title: Remove chain tensioners, chains, guide rails and chain ramps

notices.text: THE OTHER SIGNATURE M96 WEAR ITEM. The chain ramps and guides are plastic over a steel spine, and they heat-cycle themselves brittle then wear through — which retards cam timing and throws the deviation codes you logged at the start. Lay every ramp out and photograph the wear faces next to a new one; grooves worn past roughly half the pad thickness, or any cracking/missing chunks, condemn the set. ALL ramps, rails and chains get replaced on a full rebuild — they are cheap relative to doing this job twice. Retrieve the tensioner shoes and count the pieces; a missing chunk of ramp is somewhere in your engine and you need to find it.

steps.text: Remove chain tensioners, chains, guide rails and chain ramps.

fasteners.name: Chain tensioner into case

stages.label: M27 x 2: 80 Nm (59 ft-lb), tensioner to crankcase and tensioner to cylinder head alike.

fasteners.note: Tensioners are hydraulic; compress and pin before installation, release only after the chains are on. M96/01 edition value; the 3.6 tensioners carry different part numbers, confirm against the torque book page.

fasteners.name: M6 x 30 pan-head socket screws at chain box (10.9)
fasteners.note: Use a magnetic bit for the screw that enters the slot — if dropped it goes into the crankcase.
